attempts.label: DANDI:000630
attempts.entry_title: Human layer 1 interneuron electrophysiology (Chartrand et al. 2023)
attempts.description: Tests the electrophysiology findings of Chartrand et al. (2023) on dandiset 000630, which holds the current clamp recordings of the paper's 210 Seattle human L1 patch-seq cells. Features are extracted with IPFX from the long square sweeps and compared with the paper's per-cell table; cell types come from the paper's cell table, linked by the LIMS identifier. A second notebook compares the human cells with the paper's mouse L1 cells from dandiset 000020. A third notebook tests four morphology claims on the paper's deposited morphology features.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's files can be matched one to one to the cells of the paper's per-cell table, and the matched records agree on what both describe.
outcomes.source: Data and materials availability; the code's data/human_l1_dataset_2023_02_06.csv and data/aibs_features_E.csv (github.com/AllenInstitute/patchseq_human_L1 at commit 7777857c1b89b19735e45fd9c9bd7493cc1d805c)
outcomes.notes: All 210 files match one row each of the paper's cell table through the LIMS number (session_id equals the Ephys_Roi_Result number in the table's nwb_path); 204 files carry the table's cell name and 6 carry a time stamp in its place. Age agrees for all 208 cells with a known age: the files state ages as whole years times 365 days, and the one mismatch of the first run came from dividing by 365.25. The records do not all agree, so the partial level applies (at least 90% of files match and agree). One file (H19.03.321.12.04.01.04) states sex unknown where the table gives M, and the two files of donor 922967568 state an age of P0.0D where the table has none. Of the 44 features computed here, the 39 used in reading (a) agree with the paper's table within 1% for 53 to 98% of cells (Spearman 0.886 to 0.997); the five adaptation ratios not used agree for 4 to 37%. Where a feature at rheobase + 40 pA differs, the sweep chosen here is often another one than the paper's. For the initial firing rate at rheobase + 40 pA, 31 cells differ by more than 1% or have a value on one side only: 10 take another repeat of the same amplitude here, 6 another amplitude, 13 have no sweep here that gives the paper's value (5 of all cells have a different rheobase), and 2 have a value on one side only. In 16 cells no sweep passing QC lies 39 to 61 pA above rheobase and IPFX falls back to the spiking sweep closest to rheobase + 39 pA; 7 of them agree with the paper's value, and in 7 of the 9 that do not, the paper's value comes from a sweep in range that fails here only the Methods' 500 ms rms noise criterion. Without that criterion the 39 features agree with the paper's values for more cells in 38 of them (median share 0.933 against 0.895). The dandiset holds exactly the paper's primary set P (210 Seattle cells of the strict L1 set with long square features); the other 62 cells of the strict set, 50 Amsterdam and Szeged cells and 12 Seattle cells that failed feature extraction, are not in it.
deviations: The match uses the LIMS number, as no file names its t-type or the table's specimen id.

outcomes.statement: Human L1 subclasses differ in electrophysiology, notably in sag and initial firing rate (Kruskal-Wallis, FDR-corrected p < 1e-7).
outcomes.source: Results, Morpho-electric diversity in human L1, paragraph 1; Figure 2C
outcomes.quote: Electrophysiologically, subclasses were distinguished by subthreshold properties such as sag ... as well as several suprathreshold properties including firing rate ... Electrophysiological and morphological features distinguishing L1 subclasses (KW test, FDR-corrected p<10−7 for electrophysiology

statistics.n: 96 LAMP5, 35 MC4R, 33 PAX6 and 15 L1 VIP cells (Table S2)

outcomes.notes: Kruskal-Wallis across the four core subclasses (179 cells, 92 features). Sag has FDR p = 6.6e-20 (epsilon2 0.57). The initial firing rate at rheobase + 40 pA (first_isi_inv_hero) has FDR p = 4.7e-7 on the features computed here with the Methods' sweep QC, above the claim's 1e-7, and 1.7e-8 on the paper's own values (reading (b)), below it. 56 features have FDR p < 0.05. The computed initial firing rate differs from the paper's value by more than 1%, or has a value on one side only, in 28 of the 179 cells: 10 take another repeat of the same amplitude, 6 another amplitude, 10 have no sweep here that gives the paper's value and 2 have a value on one side only. In 11 cells of the test no sweep passing QC lies 39 to 61 pA above rheobase and IPFX falls back to a lower sweep; 6 of them disagree with the paper, and in 4 of these the paper's value comes from a sweep in range that fails here only the Methods' 500 ms rms noise criterion. Extracted without that criterion (variant a'), the features agree with the paper's values for more cells in 38 of 39 features, and first_isi_inv_hero has FDR p = 3.9e-9 (sag 3.3e-20), so the claim holds in full. The outcome rests on (a'), an assumption stated under deviations; with the criterion as written the claim is partially reproduced. The outcome was partially_reproduced through round 2 and was changed to reproduced after verification round 3. With any one donor left out, the largest uncorrected p is 3.1e-19 for sag and 3.5e-5 for the initial firing rate, on reading (a); this check was not run on (a').
deviations: Features follow the claims file's O1. Reading (a) uses the features computed here with IPFX 2.1.2 from the long square sweeps where they agree with the paper's aibs_features_E.csv within 1% for at least half of the cells (39 features, which agree within 1% for 53 to 98% of cells), and the paper's values for the others (custom features the paper did not release, ramp, short square and chirp features, and five adaptation ratios, which agree within 1% for only 4 to 37% of cells). Reading (b) uses the paper's values throughout. The 50% rule is an assumption of this attempt; the claims file's O1 does not say when a recomputed feature counts as computed. Two variants of reading (a) are shown, (a') with the features extracted without the Methods' 500 ms rms noise criterion, and (a, ratios) with the adaptation ratios computed here, for figs3a, fig6d and fig3g; neither changes an outcome except (a') for fig2c-subclass-ephys-differences, whose outcome rests on it.

Assumed that the paper's sweep QC did not exclude the sweeps that fail here only the Methods' rms noise criterion of 0.5 mV over 500 ms (Methods, Quality control) as IPFX measures it, so the outcome is judged on variant (a'), extracted without that criterion. This departs from the Methods' QC as IPFX measures it. The paper's own per-cell values were computed from such sweeps (7 of the 9 fallback cells that disagree with the paper), and without the criterion 38 of the 39 recomputed features agree with the paper's values for more cells (median share within 1% 0.933 against 0.895). With the criterion as written (reading a) the claim is partially reproduced (first_isi_inv_hero FDR p 4.7e-7); on the paper's values (reading b) it holds (1.7e-8). How the paper measured this noise is asked of the authors (findings, methods_unavailable).

Sweep QC follows the Methods as far as the files allow (leak within 100 pA, rms noise below 0.2 mV over 1.5 ms and 0.5 mV over 500 ms, IPFX's integrity check, and sweeps stored with zeros before the end of the stimulus left out); the Methods' criterion of a baseline within 2 mV of target is not applied, as the files do not state the target.
Dunn's post hoc tests as the Methods and legend say; the code's Mann-Whitney post hoc is computed as a variant.

outcomes.statement: Spike adaptation properties are strongly and inversely related to sag across human L1 cells (R2 = 0.74).
outcomes.source: Results, Morpho-electric diversity in human L1, paragraph 1; Figure S3A legend
outcomes.quote: Spike adaptation properties showed a strong inverse relationship with sag across the dataset (Fig. S3A)
outcomes.notes: OLS of the upstroke adaptation ratio (third over first spike, the order that matches the paper's table) on sag with HC3 errors over 192 cells. In reading (a) the ratio is the paper's value (the ratio computed here agrees within 1% for 19% of cells and is not used) and sag is computed here: R2 = 0.334 (p = 1.3e-12). On the paper's values R2 = 0.359 (p = 3.3e-14), and in variant (a') 0.346, against 0.74 +/- 0.074. With both sag and the ratio computed here R2 is 0.204 (third over first, p = 1.6e-7) or 0.149 (first over third). All the paper's ratios are below 1 (0.38 to 0.97), so the upstroke falls from the first to the third spike, and the slope is negative (-0.61 in reading (a), -0.64 on the paper's values): cells with more sag have a larger fall, so more change, the opposite of the direction the criterion states. The paper says only inverse relationship, which a negative slope matches; whether the criterion misreads the paper is asked of a reader (questions/000630.yaml), and it cannot change the outcome, which fails on R2. On the medians of the ten t-types R2 is 0.28 to 0.31. The paper's own per-cell values with the code's regression do not give 0.74 either.

findings.statement: The files carry no t-type, subclass, cortical layer, brain region or donor medical condition, and no specimen id of the paper's cell table. They can be linked to the paper's table only through the LIMS number in session_id, which equals the Ephys_Roi_Result number inside the table's internal nwb_path column; the dandiset's description points to the code repository but does not say how to link.

Six files (five of donor 1122692698, one of 1154304730) carry a time stamp such as 2021_08_17_112853 in general/source_script file_name, where the other 204 carry the cell name (for example H21.03.315.11.11.01.01).

In 145 of 210 files, 2586 long square sweeps that stopped early hold zeros for the samples that were not acquired, where NWB readers such as IPFX expect missing values. IPFX's integrity check passes them and reads the step to 0 mV as a spike, which changes rheobase and spike features unless the sweeps are left out.
bias_current is stored in pA, with a unit attribute of pA, where the NWB schema fixes the unit of bias_current as amperes; a reader that follows the schema gets values 10^12 times too large.

The two files of donor 922967568 state an age of P0.0D where the paper's table gives the age as unknown, and one file (session 977186103, cell H19.03.321.12.04.01.04) states sex unknown where the table gives M. Ages are stated as whole years times 365 days. The species is written as Homo Sapiens in 192 files and Homo sapiens in 18.

The dandiset holds only the 210 Seattle cells of the paper's primary set. The 50 Amsterdam (22) and Szeged (28) cells of the strict L1 set, which the paper uses as held-out validation (Fig. S8B) and in its LAMP5 t-type analysis, are not in it, and the paper names no other deposit of them.

The dandiset holds exactly the paper's primary set P, the Seattle cells of the strict L1 set (soma in L1 or within 40 um of the L1/L2 border) whose long square features were extracted. The 12 Seattle cells of the strict set that failed feature extraction and the other Seattle cells of the paper's table are not deposited, and the dandiset's description does not say how the cells were selected.

The donor medical condition is given in the public cell table for only 86 of the 194 cells of P in L1 t-types and 20 of the 71 reconstructed strict-set cells with an L1 t-type; the paper's code read it from the Allen Institute's donor database. The claims on medical condition cannot be repeated on the paper's cells.

Several features the claims rest on (irregularity ratio, depolarizing sag, ADP slope and voltage, sag time to peak and time constant, the ramp, short square and chirp features) come from code the Methods say will be released in a future IPFX version; it is not in IPFX 2.1.2 nor in the code repository. The adaptation ratios computed here from the Methods' definition (third over first spike on the lowest step with at least 4 spikes) agree with the paper's values within 1% for only 4 to 53% of cells (six ratios; 4 to 37% for the five not used). The authors are asked whether the feature code can be released.

The authors are asked what d' counts as high in Fig. 6A, where LAMP5 NMBR against LCP2 is said to be the only within-subclass pair with high d'. With the 2.2 grouping threshold it holds here on the features computed here for three seeds and on the paper's values for one of three; with the median between-subclass d' (2.40 to 2.62) no within-subclass pair is high.

The authors are asked whether the two-way ANOVA of Fig. 3D was run on ranks with Type II sums of squares and heteroskedasticity-corrected tests (legend and Data S4), or on raw values with Type I sums of squares, as the code calls anova_lm without its robust option. With every visual area, as the code takes the mouse cells, the AP height species effect is FDR p = 2.6e-38 under the first and 1.4e-43 under the second, on either side of the legend's 1e-38.

The authors are asked how the sweep QC criterion of rms noise below 0.5 mV over 500 ms (Methods, Quality control) was measured. Measured with IPFX on the deposited files, it leaves out sweeps from which the paper's per-cell values were computed: in 7 of the 9 cells where IPFX falls back to a lower sweep at rheobase + 40 pA and the value disagrees with the paper's, the paper's value comes from a sweep that fails only this criterion here. Without it, 38 of the 39 recomputed features agree with the paper's values for more cells, and the initial firing rate difference across subclasses (Fig. 2C) has FDR p 3.9e-9 against 4.7e-7 with it.

The Fig. S3A legend gives R2 = 0.74 for the upstroke adaptation ratio against sag. The code's regression (run_regressions, OLS with HC3) on the paper's own per-cell values over the cells of P in L1 t-types gives R2 = 0.36 (192 cells), and 0.31 on t-type medians.

For the mouse comparison (DANDI 000020 version 0.210913.1639, an outside input), 22 of the paper's 272 strict mouse L1 cells, 20 of them in VISp layer 1 and one of them a Lamp5 Krt73 cell, have no file in that version, and none of the paper's 15 mouse TEa cells does.

The paper compares human L1 with mouse VISp L1 (Fig. 3E legend; Methods), while the code's cross-species notebook (l1_cross_species.ipynb cell 5) takes mouse cells from every visual area (VISp, VISpm, VISl and others; 185 cells against 150 in VISp here). With VISp alone the AP height species effect is FDR p 3.3e-34 to 3.4e-33, above the legend's 1e-38.

Nucleated-patch voltage clamp sweeps are in 38 human files of the dandiset and 25 strict mouse L1 files of DANDI 000020, but the patch surface areas the paper's conductance densities (Fig. 3F) need, measured from images, are not deposited.

entries.description: Tests the electrophysiology findings of Chartrand et al. (2023) on dandiset 000630, which holds the current clamp recordings of the paper's 210 Seattle human L1 patch-seq cells. Features are extracted with IPFX from the long square sweeps and compared with the paper's per-cell table; cell types come from the paper's cell table, linked by the LIMS identifier. A second notebook compares the human cells with the paper's mouse L1 cells from dandiset 000020. A third notebook tests four morphology claims on the paper's deposited morphology features.
